name: Victorian (1890)
note: Varnished and oiled wooden partitions, panelled cabins, boats and hammocks on deck (the Yalu's "alleys of roaring flame", Santiago). Stripped: the woodwork and boats landed before action, as the Chinese did before the Yalu; not enough. Growth twice a furnished room's [EST].

name: Pre-dreadnought (1905)
note: Less varnished wood, more coats of paint ("war paint" burned on Alexander III). Stripped as the Russians were at Tsushima: woodwork out "as far as possible", yet Orel had 34 fires.

name: Great War (1914)
note: Stripped at mobilisation (Queen Mary, August 1914: boats, wooden fittings, furniture landed); wooden weather decks stay, wetted before action. As fitted is the peacetime ship [EST].

name: Interwar (1939)
note: Comfort back: linoleum, cork, upholstery, up to 80-90 coats of paint (Savo's inventory). Stripped: inflammables landed, the paint left on (scraping it is a refit). Magazine sprinklers (the USN's 1932 bulletin; research 10 §4.1).

name: Post-Savo (1943)
note: The USN after Savo: linoleum up, paint scraped to bare steel, cork, rugs and curtains banned, retardant fabrics (NBS berthing 240 MJ/m²); already stripped. Magazine sprinklers.
